title.narrative: DRC PCJR 2024-2026

description.narrative: The DRC PCJR 2024-2026 JR 2024-2026 focuses on North and South Kivu provinces, based on the highest needs in the country. The main objective of the 13 partners in the DRC JR is to collaboratively address the direct needs and relieve the suffering of the most vulnerable people, particularly IDPs and host communities, through a multi-sectoral approach covering WASH, Education, Protection, FSL and MPCA activities. The DRC JR focuses on the territories of Masisi and Lubero in North Kivu and on Kalehe and Fizi territories in South Kivu. Within the administrative zone of territories, the JR targets 4 health zones (HZ).

The DRCJR 2024-2026 will be implemented across four territories and six health zones in North Kivu and South Kivu with a total reach of 412.530 beneficiaries. The target group are the individuals affected by conflict. This includes, IDPs, returnees and host communities.

The Joint Response provides Food Security activities in most of the health zones. Education is promoted through WASH facilities in schools and snacks provided during catch-up classes. Child-Friendly Spaces will be created for play opportunities for children. This is for a multi-sectoral response. MPCA will be done in 1 health zone.

description.narrative: 1) Preventive measure must be built on a thorough analysis of the risks and should - as much as possible - be designed to provide concrete changes in the short/medium term. PRO-I12 - Gender based violence (Prevention, response, other)

description.narrative: 1) This indicator covers response to survivors of GBV (women, men, girls and boys).2) Appropriate response is defined as the provision of comprehensive services/assistance based on a thorough analysis of the risks faced by persons. The protection outcome of the response must be well defined. Relevant SOPs (including functional Referral Mechanism) should be followed. 3) Use the activity description field to describe what services (medical, MHPSS, legal, security, etc.), as well as SOPs in place.4) Number of persons must be disaggregated by age and sex at reporting stage.5) If action also includes prevention activities, please add a custom indicator to reflect this.In case it concerns medical care to GBV survivors, please capture this under HEA-I8.

title.narrative: Number of survivors who receive an appropriate response to GBV
WSH-I2 - Excreta disposal

description.narrative: Access: ratio (user/facility) of 1 toilet for a max. 20 people, distance < 50 metres from dwellings, or as locally agreed. Clean: regular cleaning and maintenance for public facilities.Dignified: Use of toilets respect cultural preference and is arranged by household(s) and/or segregated by sex. Unsafe facilities: unstable (unlined) pits with risk of collapse, pits accessible to vectors, pits contaminating water tables and poorly sited facilities which expose women and girls to attacks, especially at night. Functional facility: fully constructed, in working order and properly maintained, of a type and in a location acceptable to intended users, with hand washing facilities and anal cleansing material.

title.narrative: Number of people having access to dignified, safe, clean and functional excreta disposal facilities

description.narrative: Active participation of beneficiaries could lead to concrete proposals in programme design and/or on how to improve existing implementation. In the activity description/comment field, indicate how this input from beneficiaries is gathered (planned) and at mid/end-term stage, what input was received from beneficiaries and to which adaptations this has led.

title.narrative: Number of adaptations in the design and/or implementation of the JR, as a result of the input from beneficiaries.
WSH-I6 - Hygiene Promotion (awareness)

description.narrative: Hygiene promotion/awareness raising activities. Could be training, campaigns, radio broadcasts, flyers etc. Excludes the distribution of Hygiene/dignity kits that should be covered under WHS-I1.

title.narrative: Number of people reached with hygiene promotion/awareness raising activities
EDU-I3 - Safe and accessible learning environments

description.narrative: INEE Standards include: 1) accessibility, regardless of physical ability; 2) Clear marking of the learning environment; 3) appropriate physical structure and space; 4) space promoting learner-centred approaches, 5) community engagement, 6) basic health and hygiene, 7) adequate sanitation, 8) availability of sufficient, safe drinking water.

title.narrative: Number of learning spaces/schools set up or rehabilitated and equipped to meet standards
PRO-I6 - Capacity strengthening (Protection)

description.narrative: In activity description field:1) Define type of participants (population/authorities/Armed Forces/Armed Groups, etc.).2) Describe subject of training. 3) At reporting stage, the number of participants must be disaggregated by age and sex.

title.narrative: Number of participants showing an increased knowledge on the protection subject in focus
EDU-I4 - Capacity Strengthening (education)

description.narrative: In addition to general knowledge in subject matters as well as pedagogy, teachers/other educational personnel are trained in emergency life skills and in psycho-social support to create a supportive learning environment and to promote learners' psychosocial well-being (See INEE standards related to ‘Teaching and Learning’.)

title.narrative: Number of teachers and other education personnel trained
ACC-I1 - Participation

description.narrative: Participation is defined as the involvement of crisis-affected people in one or more phases of the programme: assessment, design, implementation, monitoring or evaluation. Participation does not take place when activities are carried out in exchange for a salary of 'in-kind' payment unless the affected people are involved in decision-making processes and have an impact on decisions that affect them.Please describe in the actvity description what this involvement specifically entails and in which phase of the program conflict-affected people are involved.

title.narrative: Number of crisis-affected people who are also involved in the design, implementation, monitoring and/or evaluation of the programme
LOC-I3 - Capacity strengthening (reach)

description.narrative: Please mention here the total number of national and local actors that received capacity-building support during implementation. In case more than one individual from a national/local actor participate in the capacity building activities, please only count this actor once. Note that this does not include local offices of INGOs.

title.narrative: Number of national and local actors supported with capacity strengthening
EDU-I1 - Formal Education

description.narrative: Quality implies but is not limited to: 1) a safe learning environment, 2) competent and well-trained teachers who are knowledgeable in the subject matter, 3) adequate materials for teaching and learning, 4) participatory methods of instruction and 5) reasonable class sizes. Especially in complex emergencies this should take into account a psycho-social dimension. Safe implies: people’s physical and personal wellbeing and integrity as well as to their freedom from physical, environmental, social, spiritual, political, emotional and psychological harm.

title.narrative: Number of boys and girls that access safe, quality learning opportunities (non-formal education)
EDU-I2 - Non-Formal Education

description.narrative: Quality implies but is not limited to: 1) a safe learning environment, 2) competent and well-trained teachers who are knowledgeable in the subject matter, 3) adequate materials for teaching and learning, 4) participatory methods of instruction and 5) reasonable class sizes. Especially in complex emergencies, the quality of education is closely interlinked with learners’ psycho-social wellbeing. Safe implies: people’s physical and personal wellbeing and integrity as well as to their freedom from physical, environmental, social, spiritual, political, emotional and psychological harm.

title.narrative: Number of boys and girls that access safe, quality learning opportunities (non-formal education)
WSH-I1 - Hygiene promotion

description.narrative: Regular and timely access: 250g soap/p/m for personal hygiene, 200g soap/p/month for laundry. This includes hygiene/dignity kits. Access may be in-kind or though voucher distribution or through unconditional restricted cash to enable beneficiary to buy soap (without compromising access to other basic needs). Distributed items need to be culturally acceptable i.e. take into account local practice and expectations.
